summary: Public Committee Against Torture asked the Central Elections Committee to remove Ben-Gvir's Aug. 30 Damon women's-prison campaign video, alleging unlawful use of state prison resources and harm to prisoners' dignity.
notes: Freshness recheck adds important legal context but not a current merits ruling. Walla reports that the CEC earlier in 2026 found a different Ben-Gvir detention-facility campaign video to be prohibited election conduct, ordered its removal and imposed cumulative NIS 23,000 costs/fine. That earlier precedent may be relevant but cannot be transplanted to the Damon video. No final CEC merits ruling on the Aug. 30 Damon video was recovered; preserve Pending and do not treat the complainant's Geneva-law allegation as an adjudicated finding.

summary: Ben-Gvir approved police officer Raot Rosenberg's promotion after roughly a year of withholding approval and after her administrative petition; earlier reporting said police command had unanimously recommended the promotion and no formal reason for the delay had been given.
notes: Fresh recheck confirms the underlying petition record: Israel Hayom reported on May 31 that Rosenberg said the police commissioner and senior command unanimously approved the promotion and alleged a nine-month unexplained delay; Ben-Gvir's office replied that the minister is not a rubber stamp and would examine the matter professionally. The promotion was later approved, but no merits ruling finding the prior delay unlawful was recovered. Preserve both the allegation and defense; no adverse canonical event forced.
